title: Minimal Artinian rings of definition under images and surjections
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring and $l$ a field finite as a $\Lambda$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field]. Use $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,l}$ and categories cofibred in groupoids as in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be such a category. Assume (S1): for $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ in the test category with $A_2\to A$ surjective, objects over the $A_i$ and a specified isomorphism of their evaluations over $A$ lift to an object over $A_1\times_A A_2$ with compatible isomorphisms. For $x\in\mathcal F(A)$, define $\mathcal S_x$ to have objects $x'\to x$ over inclusions $A'\subseteq A$ of $\Lambda$-subalgebras belonging to $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,l}$, and arrows the commuting triangles over $x$. Such an object over $A'$ is minimal if every arrow to it in $\mathcal S_x$ has the same underlying subring $A'$. Every object of $\mathcal S_x$ receives an arrow from a minimal object. Given $u:y\to x$ over $f:B\to A$, and $y'\to y$ over $B'\subseteq B$, transport $y'$ to $f(B')$ and compose with $u$, obtaining $f_*(y'\to y)$ in $\mathcal S_x$. Then (1) $f_*$ sends every minimal object to a minimal object; (2) if $f$ is surjective, every minimal object of $\mathcal S_x$ is isomorphic in $\mathcal S_x$ to $f_*(y'\to y)$ for some minimal object $y'\to y$ of $\mathcal S_y$. In particular the resulting map $B'\to A'$ of their subrings is surjective, and the corresponding square of objects over $u$ commutes.

source.place: Tag 06T1 (lemma-smallest-where-descends), both clauses, and the finite-length minimality argument immediately preceding it

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_\Lambda$. If some $a\in\mathfrak m$ had nonzero image in $l$, multiplication by $a$ on the field $l$ would be surjective, so $\mathfrak m l=l$. Nakayama applied to the finite $\Lambda$-module $l$ would give $l=0$, a contradiction. Thus $\mathfrak m$ annihilates $l$, and $\ker(\Lambda\to l)=\mathfrak m$ since this kernel is proper and contains the maximal ideal. Consequently $k_0=\Lambda/\mathfrak m$ embeds in $l$, and any finite $\Lambda$-module generating set of $l$ spans it over $k_0$; hence $[l:k_0]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 06GG (lemma-length), preliminary discussion of the finite residue extension; its maximal-ideal assertion here follows from Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2)

proof.text: For each test algebra $A$, its length as an $A$-module is finite by the Artinian self-length lemma. Its only maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A$, its residue field is $l$, and its contraction to $\Lambda$ is $\mathfrak m$ by step 1 and the specified residue identification. Apply restriction of length to $\Lambda\to A$ and $M=A$: the base is local, the target has one maximal ideal, and its residue extension has finite degree by step 1. It follows that $A$ has finite length as a $\Lambda$-module. This applies equally to $B$ and every test subalgebra used below.

source.place: Tag 06T1 (lemma-smallest-where-descends), preceding finite-length paragraph; Tag 06GG (lemma-length); algebra.tex Tags 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length) and 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module)

proof.text: Fix $z\to x$ in $\mathcal S_x$, over $C\subseteq A$. Among all objects $w\to x$ equipped with an arrow to $z\to x$, choose one over $D\subseteq C$ of least $\Lambda$-module length; the set is nonempty because it contains $z\to x$. These lengths are finite integers: every chain of $\Lambda$-submodules of $D$ is a chain in $A$, which has finite length by step 2. A further arrow from an object over $E\subsetneq D$ would contradict least length, since appending $D$ to a longest strict submodule chain in $E$ gives $\operatorname{length}_\Lambda(E)<\operatorname{length}_\Lambda(D)$. Therefore $w\to x$ is minimal. An arrow over the same subring is an isomorphism because the fibre is a groupoid; its inverse still commutes with the maps to $x$. This proves the asserted existence below every object.

source.place: Tag 06T1, immediately preceding paragraph: minimal objects exist by finite length; least-length argument made explicit

proof.text: Check that the image ring in the definition of $f_*$ is a test algebra. For $y\prime\to y$ over $B\prime\subseteq B$, put $C=f(B\prime)$ and $q:B\prime\twoheadrightarrow C$. The composite $B\prime\to A$ is local and induces the identity on $l$. Thus $\ker q\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B\prime}$, and $J=q(\mathfrak m_{B\prime})$ is the kernel of the surjective residue map $C\to l$, with $C/J\cong l$. The ideal $J$ is nilpotent by nilpotence of $\mathfrak m_{B\prime}$. Any $c\notin J$ has an inverse modulo $J$, and that inverse lifts to an inverse in $C$ using the finite geometric series for $1+j$, $j\in J$. Hence $C$ is local with maximal ideal $J$ and marked residue field $l$. A descending chain of ideals of $C$ pulls back under $q$ to a descending chain of ideals of $B\prime$ and therefore stabilizes; surjectivity of $q$ implies the original chain stabilizes. So $C$ is Artinian. Both $q$ and $C\hookrightarrow A$ preserve the markings and are local, as is seen by taking kernels of the residue maps.

source.place: Tag 06T1, preceding construction of the image functor; nilpotence from Tag 06GH (lemma-fiber-product-CLambda), surrounding Artinian test-ring facts

proof.text: Here is the transport, including its compatibility over $u$. Write $i:B\prime\hookrightarrow B$, $j:C\hookrightarrow A$, and write the arrows $y\prime\to y$ and $u$ as isomorphisms $\beta:i_*y\prime\cong y$ and $\gamma:f_*y\cong x$ in the transport presentation. Set $x\prime=q_*y\prime$. The arrow $x\prime\to x$ is represented by $j_*q_*y\prime\xrightarrow{c_{j,q}}(jq)_*y\prime=(fi)_*y\prime\xrightarrow{c_{f,i}^{-1}}f_*i_*y\prime\xrightarrow{f_*\beta}f_*y\xrightarrow{\gamma}x$. The arrow $y\prime\to x\prime$ is the transport arrow over $q$. This formula says exactly that its composite to $x$ equals $u\circ(y\prime\to y)$. For an arrow $y_1\prime\to y_2\prime$ over $B_1\prime\subseteq B_2\prime$, the equality of maps $B_1\prime\to f(B_2\prime)$ yields an arrow $q_{1*}y_1\prime\to q_{2*}y_2\prime$ over $f(B_1\prime)\subseteq f(B_2\prime)$, using that arrow and the composition constraints. Naturality and associativity of those constraints identify its composite to $x$ with the formula just given. Identity and composite arrows obey the same identities. This defines the functor $f_*:\mathcal S_y\to\mathcal S_x$ and proves the commuting-triangle compatibility used below.

source.place: Tag 06T1, preceding construction of f_*; Tag 06GJ (definition-category-cofibred-groupoids), composition constraints

proof.text: Let $y\prime\to y$ be minimal, and let $(x\prime\to x)=f_*(y\prime\to y)$ be its image, over $C=f(B\prime)$. Given an arrow $(x\prime\prime\to x)\to(x\prime\to x)$ over $A\prime\prime\subseteq C$, apply (S1) to $A\prime\prime\to C\leftarrow B\prime$, using the specified comparison $x\prime\prime|_C\cong q_*y\prime=x\prime$. Here $q$ is surjective, so the test-ring pullback lemma applies and $D=B\prime\times_C A\prime\prime$ belongs to the test category. The first-coordinate projection identifies $D$ with $q^{-1}(A\prime\prime)\subseteq B\prime$. The lifted object $y\prime\prime$ maps to $y\prime$, so composing with $y\prime\to y$ gives an arrow in $\mathcal S_y$ to the minimal object. Therefore $q^{-1}(A\prime\prime)=B\prime$. Since $q$ is surjective this forces $A\prime\prime=C$. This proves clause (1).

Now assume $f:B\twoheadrightarrow A$ and fix a minimal $x\prime\to x$ over $A\prime\subseteq A$. The test-ring pullback lemma gives $P=B\times_A A\prime$ in the test category. Its projection to $B$ identifies it with $f^{-1}(A\prime)\subseteq B$, and $P\to A\prime$ is surjective: lift each element of $A\prime$ along $f$. Apply (S1) to $A\prime\to A\leftarrow B$, with objects $x\prime,y$ and their given isomorphism over $A$ coming from the two arrows to $x$. Obtain $z$ over $P$ with arrows to $y$ and $x\prime$ whose composites to $x$ agree. Because $P\to A\prime$ is onto, its image ring is precisely $A\prime$, and the arrow $z\to x\prime$ identifies $f_*(z\to y)$ with $x\prime\to x$ in $\mathcal S_x$.

source.place: Tag 06T1, proof of (2), first pullback construction

proof.text: Apply step 3 in $\mathcal S_y$ to obtain an arrow $(w\to y)\to(z\to y)$ with $w\to y$ minimal, say over $B_0\subseteq P\subseteq B$. Functoriality from step 5 gives an arrow $f_*(w\to y)\to(x\prime\to x)$ in $\mathcal S_x$. Minimality of $x\prime\to x$ implies that its source has the same underlying subring $A\prime$, and the arrow is then an isomorphism. Thus $f(B_0)=A\prime$ and $B_0\to A\prime$ is surjective. Compose $w\to z\to x\prime$; the equality of its composite to $x$ with $w\to y\xrightarrow{u}x$ follows from the compatible (S1) square of step 7. This is the required commuting square, and proves clause (2) with $y\prime=w$.

lean.statement:
theorem artin_minimal_descent_transport [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [Module.Finite R k] (F : CofibredGroupoids.{u, v, w} R k)
    (hS1 : IsSchlessingerOne F) :
    (∀ (A : TestCategory R k) (x : fibre F A) (D : DescentCategory F x),
      ∃ M : DescentCategory F x, IsMinimalDescent M ∧ Nonempty (M ⟶ D)) ∧
    (∀ (A B : TestCategory R k) (x : fibre F A) (y : fibre F B)
      (u : totalObject F y ⟶ totalObject F x) (D : DescentCategory F y),
      IsMinimalDescent D → IsMinimalDescent ((descentImageFunctor u).obj D)) ∧
    (∀ (A B : TestCategory R k) (x : fibre F A) (y : fibre F B)
      (u : totalObject F y ⟶ totalObject F x), Function.Surjective (map u.base) →
      ∀ D : DescentCategory F x, IsMinimalDescent D →
      ∃ E : DescentCategory F y, IsMinimalDescent E ∧
        ∃ e : (descentImageFunctor u).obj E ≅ D,
          Function.Surjective (map (descentImageArrow u E ≫ e.hom.hom.left).base) ∧
            (descentImageArrow u E ≫ e.hom.hom.left) ≫ (descentOver D).hom =
              (descentOver E).hom ≫ u)
